$comment: Semgrep findings and scan-coverage gaps accepted with an owner and an expiry. Enforced by scripts/check-semgrep.mjs, which FAILS on any finding or newly-unparseable file without an unexpired entry.

findings.reason: False positive. The rule flags a non-literal in a console format position: `console.error(`[${ref}]`, err)`. `ref` is `crypto.randomUUID().slice(0, 8)` — locally generated hex, never attacker-influenced and never derived from request data, so no format specifier can be injected. The line exists specifically to satisfy the privacy rule: the full error is logged server-side under an opaque ref while the client receives only `{error, ref}`, so SQL detail, tokens and coordinates never reach the response. Rewriting it to appease the rule would make the logging worse.

parserLimitations.reason: Semgrep's TSX parser reports PartialParsing around line 1615, the JSX attribute `placeholder="Trail name (e.g. W&OD — Leesburg segment)"`. The construct is valid TSX that tsc and Vite both accept; the bare `&` and em dash trip Semgrep's own grammar. The user-facing copy is deliberate (the W&OD trail), so it is not being changed to satisfy a scanner. Consequence: part of MapView.tsx is not covered by Semgrep — tsc, eslint and the Playwright suite still cover it. Revisit when Semgrep's TSX grammar updates.

GENERATED FILE, never hand-edited: `npm run gen:types` writes it from the live schema. The partition (0289/0290) took it from ~1.5k to ~4.3k lines by adding space_id to 70 tables and 20 in_space_ views, and Semgrep can no longer fully parse it. Nothing here is authored code — it is type declarations with no executable statements, no I/O and no secrets, so the classes of bug Semgrep looks for cannot exist in it. It is still fully covered by tsc, which is the tool that matters for a types file: the app compiles against it on every build and the database gate fails if it drifts from production. Revisit if the file ever stops being generated, or if Semgrep's TS grammar handles it.
